claims.text: The baseline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The baseline alloy has poor structural integrity and cracks under load.
The as-cast alloy contains brittle phases at grain boundaries.
Brittle grain-boundary phases cause the alloy's low mechanical robustness.
Rapid solidification followed by short controlled annealing will produce an ultrafine, homogeneous microstructure.
Rapid solidification will suppress formation or growth of brittle intergranular phases by limiting diffusion.
Short controlled annealing will relieve residual stress without materially coarsening the refined microstructure.
The processed alloy will have predominantly coherent grain boundaries.
The processed alloy will have a minimized volume fraction of brittle precipitates.
A refined microstructure will increase crack blunting and impede crack propagation.
Microstructural refinement and phase homogenization will enhance mechanical integrity and reduce cracking.
The processing route will preserve the lattice transformations or other phase-change mechanisms responsible for the caloric effect.
Compressive strength will increase from approximately 150 MPa to 150–250 MPa or higher.
The processed alloy's caloric response will remain within approximately 10% of that of the conventionally cast alloy.
The intervention will remain effective during moderate-temperature caloric operation under applied fields, pressure, and mechanical loading.
Extreme processing or operating conditions that induce phase instability or significant diffusion could negate the improvements.
A mechanical improvement below 10%, or a caloric-response decrease exceeding approximately 10%, is defined as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The predicted strength range starts at about 150 MPa, equal to the stated approximate starting value and therefore permitting no improvement, while the falsification rule requires at least a 10% mechanical improvement.
